question: What is the main goal of health education in your practice as a midwife?

options.A: To reduce the workload of busy doctors
options.B: To shorten the duration of medical training
options.C: To help patients make informed health choices

explanation: You've got this! Health education is all about empowering individuals and communities with the right knowledge to take charge of their own health and well-being. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is health education considered a planned process rather than just casual advice?

options.A: It must only be documented in official hospital logbooks
options.B: It can only be performed by senior medical consultants
options.C: It requires structured assessment, planning, and evaluation
options.D: It relies strictly on government policy documents

explanation: Think of it like building a house—good teaching follows careful steps so you can be sure the mother or patient truly understands and can apply what you share. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which educational principle is all about repeating key messages so that patients actually remember them?
explanation: Great job! Reinforcement uses gentle repetition and positive feedback to help patients lock in new, healthy habits. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h2)

question: Why should you always match your health teaching to the cultural background of your patients?

options.A: To ensure the information is meaningful and acceptable
options.B: To comply with international nursing board regulations
options.C: To make the teaching sessions run much faster
options.D: To avoid using medical terminology entirely

explanation: When your health messages respect local beliefs and traditions, mothers and families are much more likely to trust you and act on your advice. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main reason to check what a patient already knows before you start teaching?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory hospital administrative requirements
options.B: To determine the exact cost of medical treatment
options.C: To avoid teaching things the patient already knows
options.D: To schedule the discharge date of the patient

explanation: Spot on! Checking first saves time and keeps your patient engaged because you focus right away on what they actually need to learn. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h3)

question: A pregnant mother is very anxious and crying after getting some stressful news. What should you do first?

options.A: Hand the patient a complex educational pamphlet to read alone
options.B: Report the patient's emotional instability to the hospital security
options.C: Address the emotional distress before starting detailed health teaching
options.D: Proceed with the planned teaching session to save time

explanation: Empathy first! When someone is overwhelmed or anxious, they can't process new information. Always comfort and calm them before diving into teaching. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which teaching method is best when you want to make sure a patient has mastered a physical skill, like breastfeeding positioning?
explanation: Practice makes perfect! Letting them show you right back helps you catch and correct any little mistakes on the spot. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why are visual aids like charts and pictures so helpful during community health talks in Nigeria?

options.A: They help bridge language and literacy gaps
options.B: They are required by law for all clinic sessions
options.C: They completely replace the need for verbal explanations
options.D: They prevent patients from asking difficult questions

explanation: Pictures truly speak a thousand words! They make health topics crystal clear for everyone, no matter their reading level. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is a key part of your daily role as a midwife-educator?

options.A: Assessing learning gaps and designing teaching sessions
options.C: Purchasing medical equipment for the hospital ward

explanation: You do this all the time! Finding out what a mother needs to know and planning a friendly chat or talk is a huge part of great midwifery care. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is it wonderful for a midwife to live out healthy habits in the community?

options.A: Personal health habits reinforce the educational messages given to others
options.B: It is a strict legal requirement for maintaining a nursing license
options.C: It guarantees that community members will never fall ill
options.D: It eliminates the need to conduct formal health talks

explanation: People look up to you! When you practice healthy living yourself, patients see that your advice is genuine and practical. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h5)

question: When is the best time to evaluate how well your health education session went?

options.A: Throughout the teaching process and at the end
options.B: Before the initial learning needs assessment
options.C: Exclusively after the patient is discharged
options.D: Only during the annual hospital audit

explanation: Checking in as you go lets you see if the mother is following along so you can adjust your explanation before you finish up. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h6)

question: A patient cannot quite explain how to take her prescribed malaria medication after you finish teaching her. What should you do?

options.A: Revise the teaching approach and explain the instructions more simply
options.B: Document that the patient is fully educated and compliant
options.C: Assume the patient is intentionally ignoring medical advice
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately since teaching was completed

explanation: That just means it's time to try a simpler approach! Learning takes patience, and breaking it down differently will help her get it right. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T8#BMP110_U2_T8_h6)
